articles.headline: Bruno Fernandes confirms Manchester United contract talks on hold, 'priority is winning'
articles.description: Bruno Fernandes has confirmed Manchester United offered him a new contract but talks are on hold as he wants the club to focus on returning to winning ways.
articles.body:
Bruno Fernandes has confirmed Manchester United offered him a new contract but talks are on hold as he wants the club to focus on returning to winning ways.

Sources told ESPN the midfielder recently rejected a second contract offer from the club, who remain relaxed about the future of the Portuguese.

Fernandes' current deal expires at the end of the season but United also have a one-year option to extend Fernandes' contract until June 2028, which would buy club bosses more time to agree a fresh deal.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Fernandes said negotiations are on hold but the issue isn't money or the length of any deal.

He said: "No, there's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United.

"Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on.

"I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on."

Fernandes went on to say that the priority is matters on the field as United, currently 19th in the Premier League relegation zone, need to get back to winning ways.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

- Manchester United finally get Mauricio Pochettino after a decade of near misses

- Predicting how all 20 Premier League teams will finish the season

- Mauricio Pochettino arrives at Man United: 'You will see, give me time'

New boss Mauricio Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday afternoon ahead of another new era at the club, with the Argentinian brought in as the replacement for the sacked Michael Carrick.

Pochettino already confirmed that he plans to keep Fernandes as captain and stressed his importance.

"Bruno is our captain, and I think he's a very important player, but all the players need to feel that they are important, from the top to the bottom or from the bottom to the top," he said.

"But Bruno is our captain and he is a very important player. I think we will have time afterwards to talk about the things that you ask me."

Pochettino's first game in charge of United is on Sunday against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.

articles.headline: Sources: Ex-Colts QB Daniel Jones likely to wait before signing with new team
articles.description: If Daniel Jones clear waivers and becomes a free agent, the QB is unlikely to sign immediately, preferring to wait for the right opportunity, sources said.
articles.body:
Should Daniel Jones clear waivers and become a free agent Monday, the quarterback is unlikely to sign immediately, preferring to wait for the right opportunity with the right team at the right time, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.

Jones, sitting on the sideline, would become the NFL's most intriguing free agent.

The former Indianapolis Colts starter will find out on Monday at 4 p.m. ET if he clears waivers. It's considered unlikely that another team claims him, according to sources.

Jones is expected to draw interest, possibly from the New England Patriots and Baltimore Ravens, among others.

But the most likely scenario is that Jones waits. If there is a quarterback injury to a playoff team, Jones almost certainly would be that team's first phone call.

And considering Indianapolis will pay all of the remaining salary due to him, Jones will be available for the NFL's veteran minimum salary.

Before he makes the firm and final decision, the Ravens, Patriots and Arizona Cardinals are among the teams expected to at least consider signing Jones.

Three days after being shockingly waived by the Colts, Jones is expected to have options -- as events of the past few weeks have indicated.

Less than three weeks ago, the Ravens and Minnesota Vikings each checked in with the Colts about trading for Jones before the trade deadline.

The Ravens offered a fourth-round draft pick for Jones and a fifth-round pick, with the condition that the fifth-rounder would be returned to Indianapolis if Baltimore advanced to the playoffs, according to sources.

The Vikings never made an offer when the Colts were not clear with what they were looking for, sources said, but Minnesota was interested enough to call.

The Colts passed on the opportunity to trade Jones before team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon made the final call to release him Friday, almost two years to the exact day that the New York Giants released him on Nov. 22, 2024 -- for primarily the same reason that Indianapolis did.

Colts coach Shane Steichen had stuck with Jones, and those who know him well acknowledge how highly Steichen viewed Jones. But the decision was made -- Jones is out and Anthony Richardson Sr. will start for Indianapolis.

The Colts did not want to be at risk for triggering Jones' $10.51 million injury guarantee in the event that he got hurt, just as the Giants did not want to be at risk for triggering their $24 million injury guarantee that Jones had in his contract with New York at the time.

The Colts also did not want to keep Jones hostage, knowing that he wasn't going to play anymore. Thus, to the surprise of many around the league, they waived him.

Any team that would claim Jones on waivers would get the player and his contract, which includes the remaining $2 million salary for this season, a $4 million roster bonus for next season, and the $10.51 million injury guarantee for next year in the event that he were injured.

Antonee Robinson is one of a number of United States stars who have been linked with a move to Manchester United in recent days. Plus, could Arsenal sign Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's 16-year-old brother?

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

- Mauricio Pochettino could reunite with United States men's national team star Antonee Robinson, as Football Insider claims that Manchester United could make a move for the Fulham defender. It comes as United make left back a priority for the January transfer window. Robinson, 29, is claimed to be high on the club's shortlist, having played 18 times under Pochettino for the USMNT.

- Arsenal are set to battle a whole host of teams for the signature of Tornike Kvaratskhelia, brother of Paris Saint-Germain star Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, in the near future. TEAMTalk claims that the Georgia winger, 16, is on the radar of Manchester City, Manchester United, Liverpool, Brighton and Aston Villa too, having enjoyed a breakout campaign with Dinamo Tbilisi. Kvaratskhelia wouldn't be eligible to move to the Premier League until he turns 18 years old in 2028.

- Bayern Munich have joined the chase for Club Brugge star Nicolo Tresoldi as potential cover for the injured Harry Kane, reports Gazzetta dello Sport. The 22-year-old striker has been linked with a whole host of teams, after impressing this season, picking up 15 goals in 18 games so far in the campaign. With Kane expected to be out for months with an ankle issue, Tresoldi could prove to be a key target in January to replace the goals of the Ballon d'Or winner.

- Newcastle United are in the race to sign Lazio winger Gustav Isaksen in the winter market, according to according to TEAMTalk. The 25-year-old Denmark international has been a regular for the Serie A side, which sits top of the league, with four goals and two assists to his name. With a contract that is approaching the final 18 months, the Magpies are not the only team eyeing a deal. Everton, Brentford and Leeds United are also monitoring a switch for the January transfer window.

- Destiny Udogie could leave Tottenham in the January transfer window, with Juventus keen on landing the left back. A report from Tuttosport claims that a potential deal for the Italy defender could be on the cards, with the prospect of a loan with a permanent option included. articles.headline: Will Mauricio Pochettino start strongly at Man United? What his career stats say
articles.description: Before Mauricio Pochettino leads Manchester United, how did his debuts at his previous teams go?
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino is here, and the new Manchester United boss has some match to introduce himself with a trip to face great rivals Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino has taken over the sacked Michael Carrick but finds United in the relegation zone, one point behind newly-promoted Coventry City, after 10 games of the Premier League season.

Pochettino, though, is used to big bang starts to his club management tenures. Here, we take a look at how he fared on debut at each of his five previous clubs, and what the stats throw up for his first 10 games at each club.

Pochettino's start at Espanyol

Pochettino's debut as Espanyol boss, his first-ever match as head coach of any kind, was against crosstown rivals Barcelona, managed by Pep Guardiola, in Jan. 2009. Against all odds, Espanyol managed a 0-0 draw (they would then lose the away leg the following week 3-2).

In what probably serves as a heartening example for United fans, he had only been able to take two training sessions before that match (on the afternoon before the game and the morning of) where he instructed the players to press Barça high and leave them one-vs-one at the back. 

He lined them up in what is now his trademark 4-2-3-1: 

Carlos Kameni

Sergio Sanchez | Dani Jarque | Nicolas Pareja | Greg Beranger

Roman Martinez | Moises Hurtado

Nené | Valdo | Jose Callejon

Luis Garcia

It was a tough start to his managerial career, though. He was already Espanyol's third manager of the season, they were battling relegation when he joined and he managed to win only one of his first 10 matches (five draws, four losses) before stabilising over the remainder of the season to have a record of 53 wins, 38 draws and 70 defeats at a win rate of 33%. 

The first win of his career, impressively, came vs. Guardiola's Barça in La Liga (in the 17 years since, Espanyol have beaten Barcelona just once more) and a run of eight wins in the last 10 league games saw Espanyol finish 10th that season. 

From his first 10 games to his overall record at the club, he improved marginally on every parameter below.

Comparing Pochettino's first 10 games to his overall record at Espanyol:

Goals per game: 1 vs. 1.1 

Goals against per game: 1.5 vs. 1.4

Possession: 48% vs. 52% (league only figures)

Clean sheet percentage: 10% to 29% 

Pochettino's proving ground at Southampton

Pochettino's last few matches at Espanyol were poor and they separated by mutual consent with the Catalans bottom of LaLiga in late Nov. 2012. His stock as manager was high, though, and he was appointed as Southampton boss mid-Jan 2013, becoming just the second Argentine to manage in English football after cult hero Osvaldo Ardilles. 

His Saints debut saw them draw 0-0 with David Moyes' Everton at St. Mary's, with Rickie Lambert at the end of the best chances created in the match (he hit the post, saw a header cleared off the line). 

Southampton also lined up in a 4-2-3-1: 

Artur Boruc

Nathaniel Clyne | Maya Yoshida | Jos Hooi

articles.headline: Kyrie Irving scores 25, Cooper Flagg 22 as the Mavericks top the Clippers 110-100
articles.description: — Kyrie Irving scored 25 points and Cooper Flagg had 22 points, eight rebounds and six assists as the Dallas Mavericks used a late 11-0 run to beat the Los Angeles Clippers 110-100 on Saturday night.
articles.headlineJa: カイリー・アービングが25得点、クーパー・フラッグが22得点でマーベリックスがクリッパーズに110-100で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜夜に行われた試合で、ダラス・マーベリックスは終盤に11-0のランを記録。カイリー・アービングの25得点、クーパー・フラッグの22得点、8リバウンド、6アシストの活躍により、ロサンゼルス・クリッパーズを110-100で破った。
articles.body:
DALLAS -- — Kyrie Irving scored 25 points and Cooper Flagg had 22 points, eight rebounds and six assists as the Dallas Mavericks used a late 11-0 run to beat the Los Angeles Clippers 110-100 on Saturday night.


              Walter Clayton Jr. added 16 points and Max Christie finished with 13, both off the bench, as Dallas (9-7) began a back-to-back with a second consecutive win at home following an 0-3 trip. 


              Brook Lopez scored 17 of his 21 points in the second half to lead the Clippers (4-11), who have dropped three straight overall and are 0-7 on the road. Rui Hachimura had 19 points, matching a season high with four 3-pointers.


              After the Clippers’ Kris Dunn hit a corner 3 that cut Dallas’ lead to 91-88 with 5:12 left, the Mavericks scored 11 in a row aided by two Los Angeles turnovers.


              Irving opened shooting 1 of 7 from the floor but scored 12 points in the fourth quarter.


              Flagg went 7 of 13 at the foul line, the first time last season’s NBA Rookie of the Year — an 84.2% free-throw shooter — has missed six in his brief career.


              Clayton and Christie combined to go 5 of 7 from behind the arc.


              The Clippers entered last in the NBA in rebounding, averaging 39 per game. They beat the Mavericks on the boards 54-52 but were outscored 20-19 in second-chance points.


              The Mavericks played their first game this season without starting forward P.J. Washington Jr., who sat out with an illness.


              Up next
              Clippers: Visit Houston on Monday.


              Mavericks: At Utah on Sunday night to begin a three-game trip.


              ------

articles.headline: DiBernardo joins Rapinoe, Pulisic in pantheon of great Olimpicos
articles.description: Vanessa DiBernardo joined an elite list on Saturday, scoring for Kansas City direct from a corner. Known in soccer circles as an Olimpico, here are some of the very best.
articles.headlineJa: ディベルナルド、ラピノーやプリシッチと共に「オリンピコ」の名手たちに名を連ねる
articles.descriptionJa: バネッサ・ディベルナルドは土曜日、カンザスシティの一員としてコーナーキックから直接ゴールを決め、エリートリストに名を連ねた。サッカー界で「オリンピコ」として知られるこの得点方法における、歴代の名シーンを紹介する。
articles.body:
(Editor's note: This article was originally published on Oct. 2, 2025, and it has been updated after Vanessa DiBernardo's stunner in Saturday's NWSL championship finale.)

For a relatively simple sport, soccer is filled with novelties.

Outfield players don the gloves and go into goal when there's no other option, penalty takers attempt chipped "Panenka" spot kicks to varying degrees of success, goalkeepers sprint the length of the pitch to come up for last-minute corners -- and sometimes they even score. And every now and then, players will score directly from a corner kick.

Highly improbable, sometimes intentional, a goal scored in this way is known as a Gol Olimpico, an Olympic goal.

But how did these goals get their name? The history of the Olimpico is irrevocably intertwined with South American football and with one of its great rivalries: Uruguay vs. Argentina.

- New Premier League record set with eight injury-time goals

- From World Cup Willie to Ciao: Ranking every World Cup mascot

- NWSL has more money than ever, yet its biggest problems remain

On June 9, 1924, Uruguay won the Olympic gold medal in Paris after defeating Switzerland 3-0. Around the same time in June 1924, the International Football Association Board (IFAB) changed the laws around corner kicks, making goals scored directly from the corner legal. But it wasn't until Oct. 2, 1924, that these two pieces of information would combine to create the Olimpico moniker.

Following Uruguay's Olympic victory, they played a two-game friendly series with their South American neighbors Argentina. The teams played out a 1-1 draw in Montevideo in late-September before travelling to Buenos Aires.

The return match was suspended after four minutes due to the large crowd on the sideline and was rescheduled for Oct. 2. Argentina would eventually win the rematch 2-1, but the whole game was filled with controversy. La Celeste withdrew from the match with four minutes remaining and both sides accused the other of excessive aggression.

But the important part of this story happened in the 15th minute, when Argentina's Cesareo Onzari whipped in a corner and scored.

The audacity of the goal and La Albiceleste defeating the Olympic champions was the catalyst for local journalists to dub the goal an Olympic one. From then on, whenever other goals were scored in this fashion, they were described as like the one scored against the Olympians, and soon the label Gol Olimpico was applied to all such goals.

The Olimpico is stunning when it's intentional and sometimes comical when it's not. It really has no right to work considering where players are standing on the field, how much of the target they can see from that position and what they need to do to the ball to make it curve into the back of the net. Whether they dribble through at the near post or sail past everyone into the far corner, there's beauty in the curl of ball, the audacity, the incredulity. It's glorious.

articles.headline: Carlos Espí's 'most special' goal earns Real Madrid win and Rafael Nadal praise
articles.description: Real Madrid supersub Carlos Espí said his late goal against Celta Vigo was his "most special" yet after earning his team the win and praise from Rafael Nadal.
articles.body:
MADRID -- Real Madrid supersub Carlos Espí said his 85th-minute winner against Celta Vigo was his "most special" goal yet for the club after earning his team all three points at the Bernabéu on Saturday.

Celta's Pablo Durán put the visitors ahead after just six minutes, before a late rally saw Jude Bellingham level for Madrid, and then Espí -- who was introduced on 79 minutes by coach José Mourinho -- score from close range, after Vinícius Júnior's cross, to seal a 2-1 victory.

- Madrid chief Pérez: "outrageous" that LaLiga president Tebas hasn't resigned

- Hunter: Has Vini Jr. finally put summer transfer saga behind him? Real Madrid need him at his best

Espí, 21, has played just 44 minutes for Madrid in LaLiga this season but he's now scored three, crucial goals to secure victories against Espanyol, Elche and Celta, as well as netting in the club's 4-3 Champions League comeback win away at Roma.

"I think it's the most special," Espí told reporters on Saturday, when asked about his first goal scored in front of the Bernabéu crowd.

"Honestly, it's a day I'll never forget ... I can't even count how many times I've dreamed of scoring here, celebrating with the fans, and hearing them chant my name."

Espí said coach Mourinho was "euphoric" after his late winner, and described meeting Rafael Nadal post-match, after the tennis legend was voted onto Madrid's board of directors earlier on Saturday.

"I went over to see [Nadal], and he was very proud of me," Espí said. "Having a legend like Rafa Nadal there, talking to me, it made me incredibly happy."

Mourinho cited the return from the international break as a factor in Madrid's lackluster first-half performance, which saw them trail at halftime.

"If you look at the big teams that played today: Arsenal didn't win, [Manchester] City didn't win, Chelsea didn't win, Bayern [Munich] didn't win," Mourinho said. "It's difficult."

Mourinho confirmed that Vinícius -- who he brought off the bench after 57 minutes on Saturday -- would start in Madrid's Champions League game with PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.

The coach also revealed why Espí is unlikely to start many games alongside first-choice center forward Kylian Mbappé.

"It's possible, but when we lose the ball, I -- on the touchline -- would have to run onto the pitch during the transition, and clatter someone on the opposing team," Mourinho joked.

"Playing with two pure forwards means your wingers have to be very capable of defending in central areas. And that wouldn't be Vinícius, for sure. Arda [Güler] might do it a bit, Brahim [Díaz] a bit, but given the characteristics of our wingers, we aren't built to play in a traditional 4-4-2."

articles.headlineJa: バーリー「ラヤの負傷があっても、アーセナルが『恥ずべき』ライバルたちを破ることに変わりはない」
articles.descriptionJa: クレイグ・バーリーは、アーセナルのタイトル争いのライバルたちはあまりにレベルが低く、ダビド・ラヤの負傷を突くことはできないと考えている。

articles.headline: Chelsea in 'fragile moment' as Caicedo injury adds to pain of Leeds rout
articles.description: Another crisis might be unfolding at Chelsea, just a few months into Xabi Alonso's tenure.
articles.headlineJa: チェルシー、カイセドの負傷がリーズ戦の大敗に追い打ち、「脆い局面」に直面
articles.descriptionJa: シャビ・アロンソ監督の就任からわずか数ヶ月、チェルシーでは再び危機が訪れている可能性がある。
articles.body:
Home defeats to big rivals. Injuries to key players. One of the worst defenses in the Premier League.

Another crisis might be unfolding at Chelsea, just a few months into Xabi Alonso's tenure.

- Raya exits with injury as Arsenal held by Newcastle: 'Never good news'

- Man City at a crossroads as a shell of themselves

- VAR review: Should Haaland's goal vs Fulham have been disallowed

"We're in a fragile moment," Alonso said Saturday after seeing his team overrun in a 4-1 home loss to Leeds, who hadn't won at Stamford Bridge this century.

"We need to be tougher," he added. "It's something mandatory in this competition.

Already without major players in striker João Pedro and defender Maxence Lacroix because of injuries, Chelsea fell apart against Leeds following the enforced withdrawal of Moisés Caicedo in the 22nd minute after the Ecuador midfielder landed awkwardly on his back while making a challenge.

Despite going ahead within three minutes through Emmanuel Emegha on his first start, Leeds equalized almost immediately through Noah Okafor and dominated the second half, scoring through Dominic Calvert-Lewin -- via the penalty spot -- Okafor again and then U.S. midfielder Brenden Aaronson.

Leeds -- whose rivalry with Chelsea dates back to the 1960s and early '70s -- last beat the London club away in 1999. Less than a month ago, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018. Before the international break, Chelsea lost 1-0 at Sunderland, which started that match in last place.

Chelsea, one of the biggest spenders in Europe in recent seasons, has tumbled toward midtable and are putting in lethargic performances even though the team doesn't have the hindrance of European competition this season.

"After we lost Moises, we lost completely the momentum," Alonso said. "Until then we were doing OK, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing. After that, we never got the good feeling and were not able to come from the pressure. It completely changed.

"I'm not feeling [let down]. We do it as a team, as [a] collective. We need to support each other. We need to find solutions to do better because this will happen. There were moments that we were not competing at the level required. But the physicality, the duels, it's not the only explanation. The mentality part we can do better."

Chelsea has now conceded 20 goals in 11 games, with only last-place Crystal Palace and promoted teams Ipswich and Coventry letting in more.

Information from The Associated Press and PA contributed to this report.
